memory_update.text: SPSC should remain a priority candidate for the retail_product_data_merchandising_execution node because its retail trading-partner network, recurring customer base, and retailer/supplier workflow integrations map directly to trusted retail data infrastructure.

ADV is relevant but lower quality: it provides shelf execution, merchandising, retailer services, category/space management, and analytics, but must be discounted unless software/data leverage and margin durability are proven.

DMRC is a speculative shadow candidate below the preferred market-cap filter; include only if later evidence confirms material retailer/CPG adoption of product digitization, digital watermarks, GS1 Digital Link, or item-level product intelligence.

Retail product data and merchandising execution has at least four public-market subnodes: retailer-supplier transaction networks, in-store execution services, product identity/data carriers, and inventory/order-management software.

Many pure-play planogram, syndicated retail data, product content management, and shelf-audit vendors appear private or acquired; later passes should check private-company owners, recent acquisitions, and public companies with hidden subsidiaries in these niches.

node: Retail product data, merchandising execution, planogram, inventory visibility, and shelf-compliance services
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around retailer-approved product data, shelf execution, inventory visibility, and merchandising workflows. The most relevant second-order public names are not consumer brands themselves but workflow/data intermediaries embedded between retailers, CPG suppliers, stores, and ecommerce channels. The strongest underfollowed candidate in this pass is SPS Commerce because its retail trading-network role maps closely to the trusted-data/workflow chokepoint. Advantage Solutions is a lower-quality but highly relevant small-cap services/data execution candidate. Digimarc is a speculative sub-$300M exception tied to product identity, digital watermarks, barcode modernization, fraud prevention, and item-level data. Manhattan Associates is included as a mid-cap reference/discovery bridge for inventory visibility and omnichannel execution software, though it is less obscure than the others.
